newsitem.title: USA: Chelsea Clinton chooses Stanford for college.
newsitem.headline: Chelsea Clinton chooses Stanford for college.

text.p: Chelsea Clinton, the only child of President Bill Clinton and Hillary Rodham Clinton, will attend Stanford University in the fall, joining the Class of 2001 at one of America's most prestigious colleges.
The White House made the long-awaited announcement of 17-year-old Chelsea's decision one day before the May 1 enrollment deadline set by most top schools.

"The president and Mrs. Clinton announced today that their daughter Chelsea will enter Stanford University this fall as a member of the class of 2001," it said in a statement. Chelsea had also considered Harvard, Yale, Princeton and Brown, among others.
Founded in 1891, Stanford is located in Palo Alto, Calif., about 35 miles south of San Francisco. The campus features Spanish architecture with red tile roofs and fragrant eucalyptus trees.

A highly selective university, Stanford admitted only one applicant of every eight last year. Its distinguished alumni include Republican President Herbert Hoover, former Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Astronaut Sally Ride.
"I'm just grateful that this day has come," Hillary Clinton said of Chelsea's decision on Wednesday during remarks at a ceremony honouring Peace Corps volunteers.

Mrs. Clinton had said on Tuesday night her daughter wanted to pursue a medical career, a course of study for which Stanford is acclaimed. In the United States, students wishing to become physicians take "pre-med" courses as undergraduates before going on to medical school.

"Right now she's very interested in medicine. That's something she'll see if she likes when she goes to college. She'd like to be a doctor," the first lady said in an interview on the CNN programme "Larry King Live."

Chelsea's choice of Stanford, where tuition and room and board cost just under $28,000 per year in 1996, put her on a separate path from her parents, who both graduated from Yale Law School after undergraduate work at elite eastern schools.
The president went to Georgetown University in Washington and Mrs. Clinton attended Wellesley College outside Boston.

"Both Bill and I talked with her about our college experiences ... At one point she might have considered both of our particular colleges, but I think she wanted to branch out and be her own person," Mrs. Clinton said.
A vivacious, outgoing person with a keen interest in history and geography and a love of ballet, Chelsea is now in her last year at Sidwell Friends School, an exclusive private school in Washington.
She entered Sidwell as a second semester eighth grader in January, 1993 when her father was inaugurated for his first term as president.

The Clintons have carefully sheltered Chelsea from media attention, but the public caught glimpses of her during last year's election campaign and during a trip she recently took with her mother to Africa.

On the Africa trip, she told a group of teenagers that her generation must overcome the temptation to succumb to cynicism and hopelessness. In August 1996, Chelsea was at her father's side during a whistlestop train trip with which he began his re-election campaign and eagerly plunged into the political ritual of shaking hands with voters.
